spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od19m4p2t0 ----
EXTENDS Integers
CONSTANT Total, QCap
VARIABLES shelf, held, queue
Init == shelf = Total /\ held = 0 /\ queue = 0
Request == queue < QCap /\ queue' = queue + 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, held>>
Fulfill == queue > 0 /\ shelf > 0 /\ queue' = queue - 1 /\ shelf' = shelf - 1 /\ held' = held + 1
Return == held > 0 /\ held' = held - 1 /\ shelf' = shelf + 1 /\ UNCHANGED queue
CrashDrop == queue > 0 /\ queue' = queue - 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, held>>
Next == Request \/ Fulfill \/ Return \/ CrashDrop
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<shelf, held, queue>>
CopiesConserved == shelf + held = Total
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANT Total = 3
CONSTANT QCap = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT CopiesConserved
nl:
A regional library runs a book reservation system for a single popular title with a fixed number of physical copies spread across the network. Every copy is always in exactly one of two pools: sitting on a shelf and available, or held by a patron (reserved or checked out). Patrons submit reservation requests into a bounded holding queue; when the queue is already full the system applies backpressure and refuses new requests until space frees up. A librarian fulfills a queued request only when both the queue is non-empty and a copy is on the shelf, moving that copy from the shelf pool into the held pool. When a patron returns a copy it moves from the held pool back to the shelf pool. One branch can crash silently: when it does, a queued request it was handling is simply dropped from the queue without ever touching a copy. Because requests and crashes never mint or destroy physical copies, the total number of copies must stay constant across the two pools.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of copies on the shelf plus the number of copies held always equals the fixed total number of copies.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od6m0p2t2 ----
EXTENDS Integers
CONSTANT Fleet
VARIABLES idle, busy, staged
Init == idle = Fleet /\ busy = 0 /\ staged = -1
BeginRead == staged = -1 /\ staged' = idle /\ UNCHANGED <<idle, busy>>
Commit == staged # -1 /\ staged = idle /\ idle > 0 /\ idle' = idle - 1 /\ busy' = busy + 1 /\ staged' = -1
Retry == staged # -1 /\ staged # idle /\ staged' = -1 /\ UNCHANGED <<idle, busy>>
Finish == busy > 0 /\ busy' = busy - 1 /\ idle' = idle + 1 /\ UNCHANGED staged
Next == BeginRead \/ Commit \/ Retry \/ Finish
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<idle, busy, staged>>
FleetConserved == idle + busy = Fleet
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANT Fleet = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT FleetConserved
nl:
A skyscraper elevator bank has a fixed fleet of cars, each always either idle in the shared pool or busy serving a call. Two independent dispatch controllers share that one pool of idle cars and both try to assign cars using optimistic locking: a controller first reads the current size of the idle pool, then attempts to commit an assignment only if the pool is unchanged from what it read. If another controller grabbed a car in the meantime, the read is stale, so the controller aborts and retries with a fresh read. A committed assignment moves one car from idle to busy; when a car finishes its call it returns from busy to idle. No assignment or retry ever adds or removes a physical car. So the number of idle cars plus the number of busy cars must always equal the fixed fleet size.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the count of idle cars plus the count of busy cars always equals the fixed total fleet size.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od9m6p2t3 ----
EXTENDS Integers
CONSTANT Blocks, Ttl
VARIABLES served, shed, ttl
Init == served = Blocks /\ shed = 0 /\ ttl = 0
Acquire == ttl = 0 /\ ttl' = Ttl /\ UNCHANGED <<served, shed>>
Renew == ttl > 0 /\ ttl' = Ttl /\ UNCHANGED <<served, shed>>
Tick == ttl > 0 /\ ttl' = ttl - 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<served, shed>>
Shed == ttl > 0 /\ served > 0 /\ served' = served - 1 /\ shed' = shed + 1 /\ UNCHANGED ttl
Restore == ttl > 0 /\ shed > 0 /\ shed' = shed - 1 /\ served' = served + 1 /\ UNCHANGED ttl
Next == Acquire \/ Renew \/ Tick \/ Shed \/ Restore
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<served, shed, ttl>>
LoadConserved == served + shed = Blocks
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANT Blocks = 3
CONSTANT Ttl = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT LoadConserved
nl:
A power-grid load shedder manages a fixed total number of load blocks, each either currently served or currently shed. A controller may move blocks between served and shed only while it holds a valid time-limited lease. The lease carries a remaining time-to-live that ticks down; when it reaches zero the lease is gone and must be re-acquired before any shedding or restoring. The controller can be slow but never fails outright, so it may renew a still-valid lease back to full time before expiry rather than dropping it. Shedding moves one block from served to shed; restoring moves one block back. Lease ticks, renewals, acquisitions, shedding, and restoring never create or destroy load blocks. Therefore the number of served blocks plus the number of shed blocks stays equal to the fixed total at all times.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of served load blocks plus the number of shed load blocks always equals the fixed total number of blocks.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od3m4p4t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets
CONSTANT Xfers, Cap
VARIABLES loc
Init == loc = [i \in Xfers |-> "new"]
InBuf == {i \in Xfers : loc[i] = "buf"}
Queue(i) == loc[i] = "new" /\ loc' = [loc EXCEPT ![i] = "queued"]
Admit(i) == loc[i] = "queued" /\ Cardinality(InBuf) < Cap /\ loc' = [loc EXCEPT ![i] = "buf"]
Settle(i) == loc[i] = "buf" /\ loc' = [loc EXCEPT ![i] = "settled"]
Recycle(i) == loc[i] = "settled" /\ loc' = [loc EXCEPT ![i] = "new"]
Next == \E i \in Xfers : Queue(i) \/ Admit(i) \/ Settle(i) \/ Recycle(i)
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_loc
BufferWithinCapacity == Cardinality(InBuf) <= Cap
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANT Xfers = {1, 2, 3, 4}
CONSTANT Cap = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT BufferWithinCapacity
nl:
An interbank settlement engine continuously processes transfer messages, each with a distinct identifier. Every transfer is in exactly one stage: newly arrived, waiting in an admission queue, loaded into the bounded settlement buffer, or fully settled. The settlement buffer has a hard capacity, and the engine applies backpressure: it will admit a waiting transfer into the buffer only while the buffer holds fewer than that capacity. Transfers may be settled out of order, so the engine picks any transfer currently in the buffer to settle next, reflecting message reordering. Newly arrived transfers move into the admission queue, admitted ones move into the buffer subject to capacity, and settled ones leave the buffer. To keep the engine running, a settled transfer's identifier is eventually recycled back to the newly-arrived stage to carry a fresh transfer. The safety concern is that the settlement buffer must never hold more transfers than its fixed capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of transfers currently loaded in the settlement buffer never exceeds its fixed capacity.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od0m0p6t1 ----
EXTENDS Integers
CONSTANT MaxEpoch, MaxBook
VARIABLES epoch, lockEpoch, booked
Init == epoch = 0 /\ lockEpoch = -1 /\ booked = 0
Acquire == lockEpoch = -1 /\ lockEpoch' = epoch /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, booked>>
Commit == lockEpoch # -1 /\ lockEpoch = epoch /\ booked < MaxBook /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
          /\ booked' = booked + 1 /\ epoch' = epoch + 1 /\ lockEpoch' = -1
Release == lockEpoch # -1 /\ lockEpoch' = -1 /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, booked>>
Reconfig == lockEpoch = -1 /\ epoch < MaxEpoch /\ epoch' = epoch + 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<lockEpoch, booked>>
Next == Acquire \/ Commit \/ Release \/ Reconfig
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<epoch, lockEpoch, booked>>
NoStaleHolder == (lockEpoch # -1) => (lockEpoch = epoch)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANT MaxEpoch = 3
CONSTANT MaxBook = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoStaleHolder
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler serializes bookings through a single epoch-stamped write lock. Competing schedulers use optimistic concurrency: each reads the current epoch, then tries to acquire the lock; a scheduler whose read epoch no longer matches is stale and must retry with a fresh read. Because requests arrive over the network in any order, acquisition attempts may be reordered. Only the holder of the lock whose stamped epoch matches the current epoch may commit a booking; committing records the booking, advances the epoch, and releases the lock. A holder may also abandon the lock without booking, releasing it unchanged so another scheduler can retry. The epoch may additionally be advanced by a reconfiguration, but only while the lock is free, so a held lock can never become stale underneath its holder. The safety concern is that no stale scheduler ever acts: whenever the lock is held, its stamped epoch must equal the current epoch.
SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever the write lock is held, the epoch stamped on it equals the current epoch, so no stale scheduler can commit.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od9m3p1t3 ----
EXTENDS Integers
CONSTANT MaxTerm
VARIABLES curTerm, recTerm
Init == curTerm = 1 /\ recTerm = 0
Elect == curTerm < MaxTerm /\ curTerm' = curTerm + 1 /\ UNCHANGED recTerm
Write == recTerm' = curTerm /\ UNCHANGED curTerm
Next == Elect \/ Write
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<curTerm, recTerm>>
RecordNotAhead == recTerm <= curTerm
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANT MaxTerm = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT RecordNotAhead
nl:
A power-grid control cluster keeps one shared setpoint record for a substation, and only the current leader may write to it. Each write stamps the record with the leader's term number. Leadership changes through failover: when the sitting leader is deemed unavailable a new leader is elected with a strictly higher term. The leader can be slow but never truly fails, so it may lag between writes without losing its term until a failover actually elects a successor. A lost update would mean the shared record ends up stamped with a term older than one already recorded, silently discarding a newer write. Because a write always stamps the record with the current (highest) term and elections only raise the term, the record's stamp can never regress below the current term. The safety concern is that the shared record never carries a term greater than the current leader term, which would indicate a fabricated or lost update.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the term stamped on the shared setpoint record never exceeds the current leader term.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od17m5p1t0 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets
CONSTANT Bags, MaxVotes, Quorum
VARIABLES cur, votes, manifest, delivered
Init == cur = 0 /\ votes = 0 /\ manifest = {} /\ delivered = {}
Propose(b) == cur = 0 /\ b \notin manifest /\ cur' = b /\ votes' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED <<manifest, delivered>>
Vote == cur # 0 /\ votes < MaxVotes /\ votes' = votes + 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<cur, manifest, delivered>>
Commit == cur # 0 /\ votes >= Quorum /\ manifest' = manifest \cup {cur} /\ cur' = 0 /\ votes' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED delivered
Deliver(b) == b \in manifest /\ b \notin delivered /\ delivered' = delivered \cup {b} /\ UNCHANGED <<cur, votes, manifest>>
Clear(b) == b \in delivered /\ manifest' = manifest \ {b} /\ delivered' = delivered \ {b} /\ UNCHANGED <<cur, votes>>
Next == (\E b \in Bags : Propose(b) \/ Deliver(b) \/ Clear(b)) \/ Vote \/ Commit
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<cur, votes, manifest, delivered>>
DeliveredAreCommitted == delivered \subseteq manifest
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANT Bags = {1, 2, 3}
CONSTANT MaxVotes = 3
CONSTANT Quorum = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT DeliveredAreCommitted
nl:
An airport baggage router commits each bag's routing decision only after a quorum of sorting nodes votes to approve it. Every bag is proposed, gathers votes, and once the quorum threshold is reached its routing is committed to the shared routing manifest. Only after a bag is committed to the manifest may it be reported as delivered to the destination gate. One sorting node can crash silently and simply stop casting votes; the remaining nodes can still form the quorum, so progress continues. To keep the router cycling, a bag that has been delivered is later cleared from both the manifest and the delivered set so its slot can carry a new bag. A lost update would mean a bag is reported delivered though its routing was never committed to the manifest. The safety concern is that every delivered bag has a committed routing in the shared manifest.
SAFETY PROPERTY: every bag reported as delivered is present in the committed routing manifest.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od14m3p4t4 ----
EXTENDS Integers
CONSTANT Drones, Leads
VARIABLES aloft, cap, lead
Init == aloft = 0 /\ cap = 2 /\ lead = 1
Launch == aloft < cap /\ aloft' = aloft + 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<cap, lead>>
Land == aloft > 0 /\ aloft' = aloft - 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<cap, lead>>
Reconfig == \E c \in 1..Drones : c >= aloft /\ cap' = c /\ UNCHANGED <<aloft, lead>>
Elect == \E n \in Leads : n # lead /\ lead' = n /\ UNCHANGED <<aloft, cap>>
Next == Launch \/ Land \/ Reconfig \/ Elect
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<aloft, cap, lead>>
AloftWithinCapacity == aloft <= cap
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANT Drones = 3
CONSTANT Leads = {1, 2}
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT AloftWithinCapacity
nl:
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm keeps at most a limited number of drones aloft at once, coordinated by an elected lead drone. The airspace capacity is not fixed: an operator can reconfigure it up or down at runtime as weather and battery conditions change, but never below the number of drones already aloft, so no drone is ever forced out of the sky by a reconfiguration. Leadership changes through failover: if the lead drone becomes unavailable a new lead is elected. A grounded drone launches only while the number aloft is below the current capacity, and any aloft drone may land at any time. The safety concern is that the number of drones aloft never exceeds the current airspace capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of drones aloft never exceeds the current airspace capacity.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od6m7p0t3 ----
EXTENDS Integers
VARIABLES reg, inA, inB
Init == reg = 0 /\ inA = FALSE /\ inB = FALSE
AcquireA == reg = 0 /\ reg' = 1 /\ inA' = TRUE /\ UNCHANGED inB
AcquireB == reg = 0 /\ reg' = 2 /\ inB' = TRUE /\ UNCHANGED inA
ReleaseA == reg = 1 /\ reg' = 0 /\ inA' = FALSE /\ UNCHANGED inB
ReleaseB == reg = 2 /\ reg' = 0 /\ inB' = FALSE /\ UNCHANGED inA
Next == AcquireA \/ AcquireB \/ ReleaseA \/ ReleaseB
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<reg, inA, inB>>
ShaftMutex == ~(inA /\ inB)
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT ShaftMutex
nl:
In a skyscraper elevator bank, two cars occasionally need the single maintenance shaft, a critical resource only one car may occupy at a time. Access is gated by a compare-and-swap owner register: a car may enter only by swapping the register from empty to its own id, which succeeds only when the register is currently empty. Having entered, the car occupies the shaft; it leaves by swapping the register from its id back to empty, which also clears its occupancy. A car can be slow inside the shaft but never fails, so it always eventually releases rather than vanishing while holding the register. The safety concern is that the two cars are never both inside the maintenance shaft at the same time.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the two elevator cars are never both occupying the maintenance shaft simultaneously.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od13m0p5t3 ----
EXTENDS Integers
VARIABLES phase, credit, snap
Init == phase = "idle" /\ credit = 0 /\ snap = -1
Pay == phase = "idle" /\ phase' = "paid" /\ credit' = 1 /\ snap' = -1
Read == phase = "paid" /\ snap = -1 /\ snap' = credit /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, credit>>
Dispense == phase = "paid" /\ snap = credit /\ credit = 1 /\ phase' = "dispensed" /\ credit' = 0 /\ snap' = -1
Retry == snap # -1 /\ snap # credit /\ snap' = -1 /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, credit>>
Cancel == phase = "paid" /\ credit = 1 /\ phase' = "idle" /\ credit' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED snap
Collect == phase = "dispensed" /\ phase' = "idle" /\ UNCHANGED <<credit, snap>>
Next == Pay \/ Read \/ Dispense \/ Retry \/ Cancel \/ Collect
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<phase, credit, snap>>
DispenseConsumesCredit == (phase = "dispensed") => (credit = 0)
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT DispenseConsumesCredit
nl:
A networked vending machine dispenses a product exactly once per paid transaction, an irreversible action. Its controller uses optimistic concurrency on the credit cell: it first reads a snapshot of the current credit, and commits the dispense only if the credit still matches that snapshot, otherwise it discards the stale snapshot and retries with a fresh read. Paying loads one unit of credit and moves the machine to the paid state. Dispensing requires the paid state and matching credit, then hands out the product, consumes the credit, and marks the transaction dispensed. A customer may instead cancel while paid, which refunds and clears the credit; if a read snapshot was already taken, the now-changed credit makes that snapshot stale and forces a retry. The controller can be slow but never fails, so it always eventually either dispenses or cancels. After a dispense the machine is collected and reset to idle for the next customer. The safety concern is that the machine is never in the dispensed state while unconsumed credit remains, which would permit a second dispense.
SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever a transaction is marked dispensed, its credit has been consumed to zero so no second dispense is possible.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od9m8p3t4 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets
CONSTANT Slots
VARIABLES coarse, ownA, ownB, cap
Init == coarse = 0 /\ ownA = {} /\ ownB = {} /\ cap = 2
GrabA == coarse = 0 /\ coarse' = 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<ownA, ownB, cap>>
GrabB == coarse = 0 /\ coarse' = 2 /\ UNCHANGED <<ownA, ownB, cap>>
DropCoarse == coarse # 0 /\ coarse' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED <<ownA, ownB, cap>>
ClaimA(s) == coarse = 1 /\ s <= cap /\ s \notin ownA /\ s \notin ownB /\ ownA' = ownA \cup {s} /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, ownB, cap>>
ClaimB(s) == coarse = 2 /\ s <= cap /\ s \notin ownA /\ s \notin ownB /\ ownB' = ownB \cup {s} /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, ownA, cap>>
FreeA(s) == s \in ownA /\ ownA' = ownA \ {s} /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, ownB, cap>>
FreeB(s) == s \in ownB /\ ownB' = ownB \ {s} /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, ownA, cap>>
Reconfig == \E c \in 1..Slots : cap' = c /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, ownA, ownB>>
Next == GrabA \/ GrabB \/ DropCoarse \/ Reconfig \/ (\E s \in 1..Slots : ClaimA(s) \/ ClaimB(s) \/ FreeA(s) \/ FreeB(s))
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<coarse, ownA, ownB, cap>>
NoDoubleAllocation == ownA \cap ownB = {}
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANT Slots = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation
nl:
A power-grid load shedder lets two regional controllers allocate individual shed-slots, using a two-level lock hierarchy. A controller must first take the coarse region lock, and only the coarse-lock holder may then claim fine-grained shed-slots. The set of active slots is a runtime capacity that an operator can raise or lower, so a slot may be claimed only while its index is within the current capacity. A controller claims a free slot into its own ledger, and may release slots back to free later. Coarse-lock ownership rotates: a controller releases the region lock so the other can take it. The safety concern is that the same shed-slot is never allocated to both controllers at once: the two controllers' ledgers of held slots stay disjoint.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no shed-slot ever appears in both controllers' held-slot ledgers at the same time.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od0m9p5t3 ----
EXTENDS Integers
CONSTANT Cases, MaxEpoch
VARIABLES stage, auth, epoch
Init == stage = [c \in Cases |-> "ready"] /\ auth = [c \in Cases |-> FALSE] /\ epoch = 0
Authorize(c) == stage[c] = "ready" /\ auth[c] = FALSE /\ auth' = [auth EXCEPT ![c] = TRUE] /\ UNCHANGED <<stage, epoch>>
Perform(c) == stage[c] = "ready" /\ auth[c] = TRUE /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![c] = "done"] /\ auth' = [auth EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE] /\ UNCHANGED epoch
Reset(c) == stage[c] = "done" /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![c] = "ready"] /\ UNCHANGED <<auth, epoch>>
Reconfig == epoch < MaxEpoch /\ epoch' = epoch + 1 /\ auth' = [c \in Cases |-> FALSE] /\ UNCHANGED stage
Next == Reconfig \/ (\E c \in Cases : Authorize(c) \/ Perform(c) \/ Reset(c))
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<stage, auth, epoch>>
DoneHasNoAuth == \A c \in Cases : (stage[c] = "done") => (auth[c] = FALSE)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANT Cases = {1, 2}
CONSTANT MaxEpoch = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT DoneHasNoAuth
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler governs surgeries, each of which may be performed exactly once, an irreversible action. Before a surgery can be performed it must hold a single-use authorization. The schedule is versioned by an epoch: an epoch-numbered reconfiguration bumps the epoch and revokes every outstanding authorization, so any authorization not yet used becomes void. Because a surgeon can be slow but never fails, a slow surgeon whose authorization was revoked by a reconfiguration simply re-authorizes under the new epoch and proceeds. Performing a surgery requires it to be ready and authorized; performing it consumes the authorization and marks the case done. A done case may later be reset to ready to admit the next patient into that room. The safety concern is that a case marked done never still holds a live authorization, since a lingering authorization would permit performing the same surgery a second time.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no surgery case marked done still holds a live authorization.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od13m1p3t4 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets
CONSTANT Bays, Machines
VARIABLES token, resv, owner, cap
Init == token = 1 /\ resv = [b \in Bays |-> 0] /\ owner = [b \in Bays |-> 0] /\ cap = 2
Reserve(b) == b <= cap /\ resv[b] = 0 /\ owner[b] = 0 /\ resv' = [resv EXCEPT ![b] = token] /\ UNCHANGED <<token, owner, cap>>
Commit(b) == resv[b] = token /\ owner[b] = 0 /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![b] = token] /\ UNCHANGED <<token, resv, cap>>
Release(b) == owner[b] # 0 /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![b] = 0] /\ resv' = [resv EXCEPT ![b] = 0] /\ UNCHANGED <<token, cap>>
Pass == \E m \in Machines : m # token /\ token' = m /\ UNCHANGED <<resv, owner, cap>>
Reconfig == \E c \in 1..Cardinality(Bays) : cap' = c /\ UNCHANGED <<token, resv, owner>>
Next == Pass \/ Reconfig \/ (\E b \in Bays : Reserve(b) \/ Commit(b) \/ Release(b))
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<token, resv, owner, cap>>
OwnerMatchesReserver == \A b \in Bays : owner[b] # 0 => owner[b] = resv[b]
====
nl:
A network of vending machines shares a pool of restock bays and coordinates access with a token ring: exactly one machine holds the ring token at a time, and only the token holder may reserve or commit a bay. Reserving a free bay stamps it with the reserving machine's id; committing then finalizes ownership of that bay, but only for the machine that reserved it. A committed bay may later be released, clearing both its reservation and its ownership. The number of usable bays is a runtime capacity that can be raised or lowered, so a bay may be reserved only while its index is within the current capacity. The token is passed around the ring so each machine gets turns. The safety concern is that a bay is never committed to a machine other than the one that reserved it, which would be a double allocation of the same bay.
SAFETY PROPERTY: every committed bay is owned by exactly the machine that reserved it, never a different machine.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od12m8p0t0 ----
VARIABLES coarse, pa, pb
Init == coarse = 0 /\ pa = "idle" /\ pb = "idle"
GrabA == coarse = 0 /\ pa = "idle" /\ coarse' = 1 /\ pa' = "fridge" /\ UNCHANGED pb
GrabB == coarse = 0 /\ pb = "idle" /\ coarse' = 2 /\ pb' = "fridge" /\ UNCHANGED pa
EnterA == pa = "fridge" /\ coarse = 1 /\ pa' = "cross" /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, pb>>
EnterB == pb = "fridge" /\ coarse = 2 /\ pb' = "cross" /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, pa>>
ExitA == pa = "cross" /\ pa' = "idle" /\ coarse' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED pb
ExitB == pb = "cross" /\ pb' = "idle" /\ coarse' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED pa
CrashA == pa # "idle" /\ pa' = "idle" /\ coarse' = (IF coarse = 1 THEN 0 ELSE coarse) /\ UNCHANGED pb
Next == GrabA \/ GrabB \/ EnterA \/ EnterB \/ ExitA \/ ExitB \/ CrashA
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<coarse, pa, pb>>
StationMutex == ~(pa = "cross" /\ pb = "cross")
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT StationMutex
nl:
A blood-bank inventory system has a single cross-match station that only one technician may use at a time, the critical resource. Access is protected by a two-level lock: a technician must first take the coarse refrigerator lock, and only while holding it may that technician enter the cross-match station. Two technicians compete. A technician goes from idle, to holding the fridge lock, to being inside the cross-match station, and on exit releases both locks and returns to idle. One technician can crash silently at any point: when it does, it abandons its work and its locks are freed, returning it to idle so the other technician is never blocked forever. The safety concern is that the two technicians are never both inside the cross-match station at the same time.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the two technicians are never simultaneously inside the cross-match station.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od14m5p4t5 ----
EXTENDS Integers
CONSTANT Cap, MaxVotes, Quorum
VARIABLES active, votes, pending
Init == active = 0 /\ votes = 0 /\ pending = FALSE
Propose == pending = FALSE /\ pending' = TRUE /\ votes' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED active
Vote == pending /\ votes < MaxVotes /\ votes' = votes + 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<active, pending>>
CommitActivate == pending /\ votes >= Quorum /\ active < Cap /\ active' = active + 1 /\ pending' = FALSE /\ votes' = 0
AdminActivate == active < Cap /\ active' = active + 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, pending>>
Deactivate == active > 0 /\ active' = active - 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, pending>>
Next == Propose \/ Vote \/ CommitActivate \/ AdminActivate \/ Deactivate
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<active, votes, pending>>
ActiveWithinCapacity == active <= Cap
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANT Cap = 2
CONSTANT MaxVotes = 3
CONSTANT Quorum = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT ActiveWithinCapacity
nl:
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm activates surveillance sectors, but never more than a fixed number of sectors may be active at once. Normally a sector is activated only after a quorum of drones votes to approve the proposal: a proposal opens, drones cast votes, and once the quorum threshold is reached the sector is activated, provided the active count is still below capacity. A privileged incident commander has an admin override that can activate a sector immediately without any vote, but the override still respects the hard capacity and refuses to activate beyond it. Active sectors can also be deactivated when no longer needed. The safety concern is that the number of active sectors never exceeds the fixed capacity, whether activation came through quorum or through the admin override.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of active surveillance sectors never exceeds the fixed capacity.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od0m3p5t0 ----
CONSTANT Cases, Nodes
VARIABLES leader, authorized, committed
Init == leader = 1 /\ authorized = {} /\ committed = {}
Elect(n) == n # leader /\ leader' = n /\ UNCHANGED <<authorized, committed>>
Authorize(c) == c \notin authorized /\ authorized' = authorized \cup {c} /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, committed>>
Commit(c) == c \in authorized /\ c \notin committed /\ committed' = committed \cup {c} /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, authorized>>
CrashDrop(c) == c \in authorized /\ c \notin committed /\ authorized' = authorized \ {c} /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, committed>>
Archive(c) == c \in committed /\ committed' = committed \ {c} /\ authorized' = authorized \ {c} /\ UNCHANGED leader
Next == (\E n \in Nodes : Elect(n)) \/ (\E c \in Cases : Authorize(c) \/ Commit(c) \/ CrashDrop(c) \/ Archive(c))
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<leader, authorized, committed>>
CommittedAreAuthorized == committed \subseteq authorized
====
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler commits surgeries through a single elected leader node. Committing a surgery is irreversible and may happen at most once per case. Before a case can be committed, the leader must first issue an authorization for it. Leadership changes by failover: a new leader may be elected at any time. One scheduler node can crash silently: when it does, an authorization it was holding for a not-yet-committed case is simply dropped, so that case must be authorized again before it can commit. Committing a case requires an outstanding authorization and that the case is not already committed. To recycle rooms, a committed case is later archived, clearing both its commit record and its authorization together. The safety concern is that a case is never recorded as committed unless it currently holds a matching authorization, so no commit can be fabricated.
SAFETY PROPERTY: every committed case has an outstanding authorization; committed cases are a subset of authorized cases.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od1m1p5t5 ----
CONSTANT Flights, Controllers
VARIABLES token, slot, status
Init == token = 1 /\ slot = [f \in Flights |-> FALSE] /\ status = [f \in Flights |-> "grounded"]
Allocate(f) == status[f] = "grounded" /\ slot[f] = FALSE /\ slot' = [slot EXCEPT ![f] = TRUE] /\ UNCHANGED <<token, status>>
AdminAllocate(f) == status[f] = "grounded" /\ slot[f] = FALSE /\ slot' = [slot EXCEPT ![f] = TRUE] /\ UNCHANGED <<token, status>>
Depart(f) == status[f] = "grounded" /\ slot[f] = TRUE /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![f] = "departed"] /\ slot' = [slot EXCEPT ![f] = FALSE] /\ UNCHANGED token
Pass(c) == c # token /\ token' = c /\ UNCHANGED <<slot, status>>
Reset(f) == status[f] = "departed" /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![f] = "grounded"] /\ UNCHANGED <<token, slot>>
Next == (\E c \in Controllers : Pass(c)) \/ (\E f \in Flights : Allocate(f) \/ AdminAllocate(f) \/ Depart(f) \/ Reset(f))
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<token, slot, status>>
DepartedHasNoSlot == \A f \in Flights : (status[f] = "departed") => (slot[f] = FALSE)
====
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator issues each flight its departure clearance at most once, an irreversible action. Controllers coordinate with a token ring: exactly one controller holds the ring token at a time, and normally only the token holder may allocate a departure slot to a waiting flight. A privileged supervisor has an admin override that can allocate a departure slot to a flight without holding the token, for emergencies. A flight departs by consuming its allocated slot, which flips the flight from grounded to departed and clears the slot. The token is passed among controllers so each gets turns. To reuse flight records, a departed flight is later reset back to grounded for a future departure. The safety concern is that a flight recorded as departed never still holds an unconsumed departure slot, which would let it be cleared to depart a second time.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no flight marked departed still holds an unconsumed departure slot.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od18m5p6t4 ----
EXTENDS Integers
CONSTANT MaxEpoch, MaxVotes, Quorum
VARIABLES epoch, votes, door, authEpoch
Init == epoch = 0 /\ votes = 0 /\ door = "locked" /\ authEpoch = 0
Vote == votes < MaxVotes /\ votes' = votes + 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, door, authEpoch>>
Unlock == door = "locked" /\ votes >= Quorum /\ door' = "open" /\ authEpoch' = epoch /\ votes' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED epoch
Lock == door = "open" /\ door' = "locked" /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, votes, authEpoch>>
Reconfig == epoch < MaxEpoch /\ epoch' = epoch + 1 /\ votes' = 0 /\ door' = "locked" /\ UNCHANGED authEpoch
Next == Vote \/ Unlock \/ Lock \/ Reconfig
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<epoch, votes, door, authEpoch>>
NoStaleUnlock == (door = "open") => (authEpoch = epoch)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANT MaxEpoch = 2
CONSTANT MaxVotes = 3
CONSTANT Quorum = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoStaleUnlock
nl:
A smart-home door lock network opens the front door only when a quorum of currently enrolled devices endorses the unlock. Device enrollment is a runtime capacity that changes as devices are added or removed; every such enrollment change advances an epoch, re-locks the door, and invalidates any votes cast under the old epoch, so a stale device holding an outdated credential can never contribute to an unlock. Enrolled devices cast votes in the current epoch; once the quorum threshold is reached the door opens and records the epoch under which it was authorized, consuming the votes. The door can later be locked again. The safety concern is that whenever the door is open, it was authorized under the current epoch, so no stale or unauthorized device ever causes an open.
SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever the door is open, the epoch under which it was authorized equals the current epoch.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od2m1p4t3 ----
EXTENDS Integers
CONSTANT Robots, Cap
VARIABLES token, inZone
Init == token = 1 /\ inZone = 0
Admit == inZone < Cap /\ inZone' = inZone + 1 /\ UNCHANGED token
Leave == inZone > 0 /\ inZone' = inZone - 1 /\ UNCHANGED token
Pass == \E r \in Robots : r # token /\ token' = r /\ UNCHANGED inZone
Next == Admit \/ Leave \/ Pass
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<token, inZone>>
ZoneWithinCapacity == inZone <= Cap
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANT Robots = {1, 2, 3}
CONSTANT Cap = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT ZoneWithinCapacity
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet shares a charging zone that holds only a limited number of robots at once. A token ring coordinates admission: exactly one robot holds the ring token at a time, and only the token holder may admit itself into the charging zone, and only while the zone is below its capacity. A robot in the zone may leave at any time, freeing a slot. A robot can be slow to finish charging but never fails, so it always eventually leaves rather than occupying a slot forever. The token is passed around the ring so admission rights rotate among robots. The safety concern is that the number of robots in the charging zone never exceeds its capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of robots in the charging zone never exceeds the zone capacity.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od12m7p2t1 ----
EXTENDS Integers
CONSTANT Total, Requesters
VARIABLES stored, issued, reg
Init == stored = Total /\ issued = 0 /\ reg = 0
Claim == \E r \in Requesters : reg = 0 /\ reg' = r /\ UNCHANGED <<stored, issued>>
IssueUnit == reg # 0 /\ stored > 0 /\ stored' = stored - 1 /\ issued' = issued + 1 /\ reg' = 0
ReturnUnit == reg # 0 /\ issued > 0 /\ issued' = issued - 1 /\ stored' = stored + 1 /\ reg' = 0
Next == Claim \/ IssueUnit \/ ReturnUnit
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<stored, issued, reg>>
UnitsConserved == stored + issued = Total
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANT Total = 3
CONSTANT Requesters = {1, 2}
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT UnitsConserved
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker holds a fixed total number of blood units, each either in cold storage or issued to a ward. Transfer requests from multiple wards arrive over the network in any order. A single compare-and-swap transfer register serializes them: a requester claims the register by swapping it from free to its own id, which succeeds only when the register is free. The holder then performs exactly one move, either issuing a unit from storage to a ward or returning a unit from a ward to storage, and the move releases the register back to free. No claim, issue, or return ever creates or destroys a unit. Therefore the number of units in cold storage plus the number issued always equals the fixed total.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of units in cold storage plus the number issued always equals the fixed total number of units.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od9m4p3t5 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets
CONSTANT Slots, QCap
VARIABLES reserved, allocated, qcount
Init == reserved = {} /\ allocated = {} /\ qcount = 0
Enqueue(s) == qcount < QCap /\ s \notin reserved /\ s \notin allocated /\ reserved' = reserved \cup {s} /\ qcount' = qcount + 1 /\ UNCHANGED allocated
Commit(s) == s \in reserved /\ reserved' = reserved \ {s} /\ allocated' = allocated \cup {s} /\ qcount' = qcount - 1
AdminAlloc(s) == s \notin reserved /\ s \notin allocated /\ allocated' = allocated \cup {s} /\ UNCHANGED <<reserved, qcount>>
Free(s) == s \in allocated /\ allocated' = allocated \ {s} /\ UNCHANGED <<reserved, qcount>>
Next == \E s \in Slots : Enqueue(s) \/ Commit(s) \/ AdminAlloc(s) \/ Free(s)
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<reserved, allocated, qcount>>
NoDoubleAllocation == reserved \cap allocated = {}
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANT Slots = {1, 2, 3}
CONSTANT QCap = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation
nl:
A power-grid load shedder allocates individual shed-slots through a bounded work queue with backpressure. A shed request reserves a target slot and enters the queue, but only while the queue is below its capacity and the slot is neither already reserved nor already allocated; when the queue is full the system applies backpressure and refuses new reservations. Dequeuing a reserved request commits its slot into the allocated set and frees a queue position. A privileged grid operator has an admin override that can allocate a free slot directly, bypassing the queue, but only for a slot that is neither reserved nor already allocated. Allocated slots can later be freed. The safety concern is that no slot is ever both reserved in the queue and allocated at the same time, which would be a double allocation of that slot.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no shed-slot is ever simultaneously reserved in the queue and present in the allocated set.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od1m9p0t5 ----
EXTENDS Integers
CONSTANT MaxEpoch
VARIABLES onA, onB, epoch
Init == onA = FALSE /\ onB = FALSE /\ epoch = 0
EnterA == ~onA /\ ~onB /\ onA' = TRUE /\ UNCHANGED <<onB, epoch>>
EnterB == ~onA /\ ~onB /\ onB' = TRUE /\ UNCHANGED <<onA, epoch>>
ExitA == onA /\ onA' = FALSE /\ UNCHANGED <<onB, epoch>>
ExitB == onB /\ onB' = FALSE /\ UNCHANGED <<onA, epoch>>
Reconfig == ~onA /\ ~onB /\ epoch < MaxEpoch /\ epoch' = epoch + 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<onA, onB>>
AdminClear == onA' = FALSE /\ onB' = FALSE /\ UNCHANGED epoch
Next == EnterA \/ EnterB \/ ExitA \/ ExitB \/ Reconfig \/ AdminClear
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<onA, onB, epoch>>
RunwayMutex == ~(onA /\ onB)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANT MaxEpoch = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT RunwayMutex
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator manages a single runway, a critical resource that at most one flight may occupy at a time. A flight may enter the runway only when it is completely clear, and it exits when its operation finishes. The runway configuration is versioned by an epoch: an epoch-numbered reconfiguration, such as a direction change, may occur only while the runway is clear, advancing the epoch. A privileged supervisor has an admin override that can force the runway clear in an emergency, evicting whichever flight is on it. The safety concern is that two flights are never both on the runway at the same time.
SAFETY PROPERTY: two flights are never simultaneously occupying the runway.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od19m3p4t0 ----
EXTENDS Integers
CONSTANT Nodes, Cap
VARIABLES leader, holds
Init == leader = 1 /\ holds = 0
Elect == \E n \in Nodes : n # leader /\ leader' = n /\ UNCHANGED holds
Grant == holds < Cap /\ holds' = holds + 1 /\ UNCHANGED leader
Release == holds > 0 /\ holds' = holds - 1 /\ UNCHANGED leader
CrashDrop == holds > 0 /\ holds' = holds - 1 /\ UNCHANGED leader
Next == Elect \/ Grant \/ Release \/ CrashDrop
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<leader, holds>>
HoldsWithinCapacity == holds <= Cap
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANT Nodes = {1, 2}
CONSTANT Cap = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT HoldsWithinCapacity
nl:
A library book reservation system for a scarce title keeps at most a fixed number of active reservation holds outstanding at once. An elected leader node grants new holds, but only while the number of active holds is below the capacity; holds may be released when patrons pick up or cancel. Leadership changes by failover: a new leader may be elected at any time. One node can crash silently: when it does, an active hold it was tracking is silently dropped, decrementing the count of outstanding holds. The safety concern is that the number of outstanding reservation holds never exceeds the fixed capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of outstanding reservation holds never exceeds the fixed capacity.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od8m0p2t5 ----
EXTENDS Integers
CONSTANT Total
VARIABLES avail, enrolled, snap
Init == avail = Total /\ enrolled = 0 /\ snap = -1
Read == snap = -1 /\ snap' = avail /\ UNCHANGED <<avail, enrolled>>
Enroll == snap = avail /\ avail > 0 /\ avail' = avail - 1 /\ enrolled' = enrolled + 1 /\ snap' = -1
Retry == snap # -1 /\ snap # avail /\ snap' = -1 /\ UNCHANGED <<avail, enrolled>>
Drop == enrolled > 0 /\ enrolled' = enrolled - 1 /\ avail' = avail + 1 /\ UNCHANGED snap
AdminEnroll == avail > 0 /\ avail' = avail - 1 /\ enrolled' = enrolled + 1 /\ UNCHANGED snap
Next == Read \/ Enroll \/ Retry \/ Drop \/ AdminEnroll
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<avail, enrolled, snap>>
SeatsConserved == avail + enrolled = Total
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANT Total = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT SeatsConserved
nl:
A university course-registration system manages a single course with a fixed total number of seats; every seat is either available or enrolled. Students register using optimistic concurrency on the available-seat count: a student first reads a snapshot of the current available count, then commits an enrollment only if the count still matches that snapshot, decrementing available and incrementing enrolled. If a concurrent change made the snapshot stale, the student discards it and retries with a fresh read. A student may also drop the course, moving a seat from enrolled back to available, which can invalidate an outstanding snapshot and force a retry. A privileged registrar has an admin override that force-enrolls a student directly whenever a seat is available, bypassing the optimistic check. No registration, drop, retry, or override ever creates or destroys a seat. Therefore the number of available seats plus the number of enrolled seats always equals the fixed total.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of available seats plus the number of enrolled seats always equals the fixed total number of seats.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od19m1p3t5 ----
CONSTANT Copies
VARIABLES token, heldA, heldB
Init == token = 1 /\ heldA = {} /\ heldB = {}
HoldA(c) == token = 1 /\ c \notin heldA /\ c \notin heldB /\ heldA' = heldA \cup {c} /\ UNCHANGED <<token, heldB>>
HoldB(c) == token = 2 /\ c \notin heldA /\ c \notin heldB /\ heldB' = heldB \cup {c} /\ UNCHANGED <<token, heldA>>
AdminHoldA(c) == c \notin heldA /\ c \notin heldB /\ heldA' = heldA \cup {c} /\ UNCHANGED <<token, heldB>>
AdminHoldB(c) == c \notin heldA /\ c \notin heldB /\ heldB' = heldB \cup {c} /\ UNCHANGED <<token, heldA>>
ReleaseA(c) == c \in heldA /\ heldA' = heldA \ {c} /\ UNCHANGED <<token, heldB>>
ReleaseB(c) == c \in heldB /\ heldB' = heldB \ {c} /\ UNCHANGED <<token, heldA>>
Pass == token' = (IF token = 1 THEN 2 ELSE 1) /\ UNCHANGED <<heldA, heldB>>
Next == Pass \/ (\E c \in Copies : HoldA(c) \/ HoldB(c) \/ AdminHoldA(c) \/ AdminHoldB(c) \/ ReleaseA(c) \/ ReleaseB(c))
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<token, heldA, heldB>>
LedgersDisjoint == heldA \cap heldB = {}
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANT Copies = {1, 2, 3}
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT LedgersDisjoint
nl:
A library book reservation system lets two branches place holds on individual copies of a title, coordinating through a token ring so that exactly one branch holds the ring token at a time. Normally only the token holder may place a hold on a copy, and only on a copy that neither branch currently holds. Each branch records the copies it holds in its own ledger. A copy on hold may later be released back to free. A privileged headquarters has an admin override that can place a hold on any currently-free copy on behalf of either branch without waiting for the token. The token is passed between the two branches so hold rights alternate. The safety concern is that the same copy is never held by both branches at once: the two branches' ledgers of held copies stay disjoint.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no copy ever appears in both branches' held-copy ledgers at the same time.
